meta.purpose: Determine whether an organisation has a material, quantifiable FinOps problem — and make the cost of inaction visible to an executive who has not yet accepted it. This is a qualification instrument, not a maturity assessment. The headline output is money at stake, not a score.
meta.audience: BU owners, CTO, Technology Directors, Cloud Programme leads, CFO-adjacent technology finance roles
meta.disclaimer: Indicative estimate based on self-reported inputs and published industry benchmarks. Figures illustrate the scale of opportunity and are not a guarantee of savings. A validated baseline requires an assessment of actual billing data.
design_principles: Don't know is a scored answer, never a skip. It scores worst-case and increments a blind-spot counter surfaced in the report.
The headline output is a currency range, not an index.
Capability gap and commercial urgency are scored separately, then combined.
Every weak signal maps to a named LTM service area with concrete deliverables — no generic recommendations.

signals.label: Scale & trajectory
signals.desc: Size of estate, growth rate and migration still ahead. Drives exposure, not gap.

signals.label: Cost visibility
signals.desc: Can spend be attributed, explained and traced to a business unit or unit of output?

signals.label: Bill predictability
signals.desc: Forecast accuracy, variance history and ability to explain movements.

signals.label: Ownership & accountability
signals.desc: Whether anyone is genuinely accountable, and whether engineers see cost consequences.

signals.label: Controls & optimisation
signals.desc: Whether mechanisms exist to prevent and reclaim waste.

signals.label: Value realisation
signals.desc: Whether cloud spend can be defended as delivering business value.

scoring.answer_normalisation: Every answer normalises to a 0-100 health score. Gap contribution = 100 - health.
scoring.gap_index: Weighted mean of the five gap signals, expressed 0-100 where higher = larger capability gap.
scoring.urgency_index: Derived from growth rate, proportion of estate still to migrate, variance volatility and surprise-bill frequency. 0-100.
scoring.need_index: 0.6 * gap_index + 0.4 * urgency_index, rounded. Higher = greater need for FinOps.
scoring.dont_know_handling: Scores 0 health (worst case) and increments blind_spot_count. Blind spots are reported separately and named individually.
scoring.confidence: If blind_spot_count >= 6, the report labels the estimate 'low confidence' and states that a billing-data baseline is required before figures can be relied upon.

benchmarks.honesty_note: Published waste benchmarks are reported cross-industry, not per-sector. The headline anchors below are global figures from named public sources. The BFSI modifiers that follow are LTIMindtree directional adjustments based on sector characteristics — they are not published sector waste rates and are marked editable so they can be replaced with LTM's own engagement data.

sources.label: Flexera 2026 State of the Cloud Report

figures.commitment_discount_uptake: fewer than half of organisations use any one commitment discount per cloud provider

sources.note: Waste rose to 29% in 2026, the first increase in five years, attributed to AI workloads and new PaaS/SaaS pricing complexity.

sources.label: Flexera State of the Cloud, multi-year
sources.note: Estimated waste has remained within a 27-32% band every year since 2019 — the most stable benchmark available.

sources.label: Harness Cloud Cost Management Report
sources.note: A more conservative estimate limited to unused or underused infrastructure; useful as a floor.

sources.label: FinOps Foundation, State of FinOps 2026
sources.note: Workload optimisation and waste reduction remain the top practitioner priority, but practitioners report diminishing returns — the large obvious waste has been captured, leaving a high volume of smaller opportunities requiring more effort.

benchmarks.anchor_logic: The Flexera 29% figure is an average across a population in which 63% already run an established FinOps team and 71% operate a CCoE. An organisation with no FinOps function therefore sits materially above that average, and one with mature controls materially below it. The bands below are calibrated on that reasoning rather than applying 29% uniformly.

bfsi_modifiers.basis: LTIMindtree directional adjustment — replace with engagement data when available

factors.label: Elevated non-production estate
factors.rationale: Regulatory testing, UAT, model validation and parallel-run environments create a larger idle footprint than in other sectors.

factors.label: Mandated DR and resilience duplication
factors.rationale: Operational resilience requirements (DORA, FCA/PRA, local equivalents) mandate standby capacity that is provisioned but rarely consumed.

factors.label: Data residency and sovereignty constraints
factors.rationale: Limits the ability to arbitrage across regions or use lower-cost capacity, and constrains commitment flexibility.

factors.label: Core system lift-and-shift patterns
factors.rationale: Migrated core banking, payments and policy administration systems frequently retain data-centre sizing assumptions rather than cloud-native elasticity.

factors.label: Extended change control cycles
factors.rationale: Rightsizing and decommissioning actions move through governance more slowly, so identified waste persists longer before it is reclaimed.

factors.label: Conservative commitment purchasing
factors.rationale: Budget governance and multi-year approval cycles suppress commitment coverage, leaving predictable workloads on on-demand rates.

bfsi_modifiers.application: Modifiers are applied to the upper bound of the derived band only, capped so the total never exceeds 45%. This keeps the headline defensible while reflecting that BFSI estates carry structural inefficiency other sectors do not.

waste_model.note: Waste rate is derived from the organisation's own visibility and control answers, then anchored to the published benchmarks above. It is never asserted as a flat percentage.

bands.label: No effective cost management
bands.anchor: Above the 29% cross-industry average, since that average includes a majority with established FinOps teams.

bands.label: Partial controls in place
bands.anchor: Approaching the Harness 21% floor for unused and underused infrastructure.

bands.label: Established controls
bands.anchor: Consistent with practitioners reporting diminishing returns once the large waste has been captured.

waste_model.bfsi_uplift: Apply the sum of applicable BFSI modifiers to waste_high only, capped at 0.45 total.
waste_model.exposure_36m: Three-year cumulative applying the stated annual growth rate at the same waste band. Presented as the cost of a three-year delay, which is the figure that moves budget.
waste_model.presentation: Always a range, never a point estimate. Always paired with the confidence label and the named source of the anchor benchmark. Never present as a guaranteed saving.

verdict_bands.label: Lightweight practices sufficient
verdict_bands.headline: No material FinOps gap at current scale
verdict_bands.narrative: At the current estate size and growth rate, formal FinOps investment is difficult to justify. Maintain basic budget alerting and revisit when spend or migration pace increases.

verdict_bands.label: Establish foundations now
verdict_bands.headline: Foundations needed before the estate grows
verdict_bands.narrative: The estate is approaching the scale where informal cost management stops working. Establishing visibility and ownership now is materially cheaper than retrofitting them later.

verdict_bands.label: Material exposure — act this year
verdict_bands.headline: A quantifiable amount of spend is unmanaged
verdict_bands.narrative: Cost is being incurred faster than it can be explained or controlled. The gap is large enough to be visible in financial results and will widen as migration continues.

verdict_bands.label: Urgent — significant value leaking
verdict_bands.headline: Spend is running substantially ahead of control
verdict_bands.narrative: The combination of scale, growth and absent controls means a significant proportion of cloud investment is not producing recoverable value. This is normally visible to Finance before it is visible to Technology.

service_areas.name: FinOps Operating Model & Governance
service_areas.problem: No one is genuinely accountable for cloud spend, so decisions default to whoever notices the bill.
deliverables: FinOps charter and mandate, signed at executive level
Operating model design — centralised, federated or hybrid, with a rationale
RACI across Engineering, Finance, Procurement and BU owners
Governance forum design, cadence and decision rights
Tooling assessment and platform recommendation
90-day mobilisation plan with named owners

service_areas.name: Cost Visibility & Allocation
service_areas.problem: Spend cannot be attributed to a team, product or customer, so no one can be held to it.
deliverables: Tagging and metadata taxonomy with enforcement policy
Cost allocation model including shared-cost treatment
Showback design, progressing to chargeback where appropriate
Executive and team-level cost dashboards
Automated cost data pipeline into the enterprise BI platform
Allocation coverage baseline and improvement roadmap

service_areas.name: Forecasting, Budgets & Anomaly Control
service_areas.problem: The bill cannot be predicted, so Finance treats cloud as uncontrolled spend.
deliverables: Driver-based forecasting model with documented assumptions
Budget framework at BU and product level with forecast-breach alerting
Anomaly detection configuration and escalation routing
Monthly variance reporting pack and commentary standard
Forecast accuracy baseline and improvement target

service_areas.name: Commitment & Rate Optimisation
service_areas.problem: Paying on-demand rates for predictable, steady-state workloads.
deliverables: Commitment coverage analysis across providers
Commitment strategy and purchase calendar
Savings plan and reserved capacity portfolio design
Provider agreement and discount review
Ongoing coverage monitoring and renewal governance

service_areas.name: Workload & Architecture Optimisation
service_areas.problem: Resources are oversized, idle or orphaned, and nothing systematically reclaims them.
deliverables: Rightsizing assessment with prioritised savings backlog
Waste and orphaned-resource elimination programme
Storage tiering and lifecycle policy design
Non-production scheduling and automated parking
Spot and transient capacity adoption strategy
Architecture cost review standard for design gates

service_areas.name: Unit Economics & Value Realisation
service_areas.problem: Cloud spend cannot be defended to the board because its business value is not measured.
deliverables: Unit metric definition per product or service line
Cost-per-unit instrumentation and trending
Cloud business case validation against original assumptions
Margin and cost-to-serve analysis by customer or tenant
Board-level cloud value reporting pack

service_areas.name: FinOps Enablement & Capability Build
service_areas.problem: Cost awareness does not survive contact with delivery pressure unless it is built into how engineers work.
deliverables: FinOps role definitions and target capability model
Training curriculum and FinOps certification pathway
Cost-aware architecture and design standards
Engineering enablement — cost feedback in CI/CD and pull requests
Community of practice launch and operating rhythm

questions.text: Which best describes your infrastructure today?
questions.hint: Pick the closest match — precision is not required.

questions.text: Which cloud platforms are in use or planned?
questions.hint: Multi-cloud materially increases the cost of poor visibility.

derived.multi_cloud_penalty: If 2+ hyperscalers selected, add 8 to urgency_index

questions.text: Roughly what is your annual cloud spend?
questions.hint: An order-of-magnitude estimate is enough. This drives the value calculation.
questions.dont_know_blind_spot: Annual cloud spend is not known to a single figure — usually a sign that spend is fragmented across accounts or business units.

questions.text: Where are you in your cloud journey?
How do you expect cloud spend to change over the next 12 months?

derived.urgency: Growth above 30% adds to urgency_index proportionally

questions.text: What proportion of your remaining estate is still to move to cloud in the next 24 months?
questions.hint: Migrating on top of weak cost controls multiplies the problem rather than adding to it.

questions.text: Can you attribute cloud cost to a specific business unit, product or team?

options.label: Only at a very high level
No — it is one undifferentiated bill

questions.dont_know_blind_spot: Cost attribution capability is unknown — meaning no one has recently tried to answer 'who spent this?'

questions.text: What percentage of your cloud resources carry complete, reliable tags or labels?
questions.dont_know_blind_spot: Tag coverage is unknown. Without it, every allocation and showback figure is an estimate.

questions.text: How long does it take to answer the question "why did the bill go up last month?"
questions.hint: This is the single most revealing question in the assessment.

options.label: Same day — the data is at hand
Weeks, and the answer is contested

questions.text: Do you know what it costs to serve one customer, transaction or unit of output?
questions.dont_know_blind_spot: Unit cost is unknown — cloud spend cannot currently be connected to business volume.

questions.text: Which of these do you receive on a regular, scheduled basis?
questions.hint: Select all that genuinely arrive without being chased.

options.label: Monthly cost report by team or product

questions.text: Over the last 12 months, how far did actual cloud spend differ from what was budgeted?
questions.dont_know_blind_spot: Budget variance is not tracked, so overspend is discovered rather than predicted.

questions.text: How often has an unexpected cloud bill required explanation to Finance or the board?

derived.urgency: 'A few times' or 'recurring' adds to urgency_index

questions.text: How confident are you in your cloud spend forecast for next quarter?
Who explains the cloud bill to Finance or the CFO?

options.label: A dedicated cost owner with the data to back it
No one — Finance interprets it themselves

questions.text: Who is formally accountable for cloud spend?

options.label: A named FinOps owner or team with a mandate
Each business unit owns its own consumption
The CIO or CTO, by default rather than design

questions.text: Distribute 100 points across where responsibility for cloud cost actually sits today.
questions.hint: Not where it should sit — where it genuinely does.

scoring.rule: score = 100 - (nobody * 1.6) - (concentration_penalty). Concentration penalty applies where one bucket exceeds 70, since sole ownership without engineering involvement rarely holds.

blind_spot_if.text: A meaningful share of cloud cost responsibility is unassigned by the organisation's own account.

questions.text: To what extent do engineers see the cost consequences of what they build?
Is cost efficiency written into anyone's objectives or performance measures?
questions.dont_know_blind_spot: No one is certain whether cost efficiency is anyone's objective — which usually means it is not.

questions.text: Which cost controls are actually operating today?
questions.hint: Select only those in live use, not those planned or configured but ignored.

questions.text: What proportion of eligible spend is covered by commitments — reserved instances, savings plans or committed use discounts?
questions.dont_know_blind_spot: Commitment coverage is unknown — typically the single largest immediately addressable saving.

questions.text: When did you last systematically decommission unused or idle resources?

options.label: Never, or not that we know of

questions.text: Rank these cost concerns by how much they worry you — most concerning first.
questions.hint: This shapes where we focus, and is not scored against a right answer.
options: Inability to attribute cost to teams
Justifying cloud value to the board

scoring.use: Ordering drives the emphasis and ordering of the LTM service recommendations in the report.

options.label: The question has not been asked yet

There was no formal business case

questions.dont_know_blind_spot: Performance against the original cloud business case is not tracked.

questions.text: If Finance asked today whether cloud spend was under control, how comfortable would you be answering?
What would a good outcome look like in 12 months?
questions.hint: Used to shape the recommendations, not scored.

A position we can defend to Finance

report_outline.content: Currency range for 12 months and 3 years, confidence label, waste band rationale. Leads the report — this is the number the reader remembers.
Need Index, verdict band, and a narrative naming what specifically drives it.
Every 'don't know' answer named individually, framed as decisions being made without data. Omitted entirely if there are none.
Five gap signals as bars, with the weakest two called out.
Only the service areas whose triggers fired, ordered by the client's own ranking from C4. Each with the problem statement and concrete deliverables.
Case studies filtered by relevance_signals matching the client's weakest signals, each downloadable.
A named, scoped first engagement — typically a two-week baseline assessment — plus the service brochure download.
